mn134:5.3: “Sir, one time I was staying in the Sakyan country at Kapilavatthu in the Banyan Tree Monastery.
mn134:5.4: Then, sir, late at night, a certain glorious godling, lighting up the entire Banyan Tree Monastery, went up to me and stood to one side. Standing to one side, he said to me:
mn134:5.5: ‘Mendicant, do you remember the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night?’
mn134:5.6: When he said this, sir, I said to that godling:
mn134:5.10: But do you remember just the verses on the one who has one fine night?’
mn134:5.14: ‘How do you remember the verses on the one who has one fine night?’
mn134:5.15: ‘This one time, the Buddha was staying among the gods of the thirty-three at the root of the Orchid Tree on the stone spread with a cream rug.
mn134:5.16: There he taught the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night to the gods of the thirty-three:
mn134:5.19: that’s who has one fine night—
mn134:5.21: That’s how I remember the verses of the one who has one fine night.
mn134:5.22: Learn the summary recital and the analysis of the one who has one fine night, mendicant,
mn134:5.25: It is beneficial and relevant to the fundamentals of the spiritual life.’
mn134:5.26: That is what that godling said, sir,
mn134:8-13.2: That’s how you run back to the past.
mn134:8-13.3: And how do you not run back to the past? …
mn134:8-13.4: That’s how you don’t run back to the past.
mn134:8-13.5: And how do you anticipate the future? …
mn134:8-13.6: That’s how you anticipate the future.
mn134:8-13.7: And how do you not anticipate the future? …
mn134:8-13.8: That’s how you don’t anticipate the future.
mn134:8-13.9: And how do you falter amid presently arisen phenomena? …
mn134:8-13.10: That’s how you falter amid presently arisen phenomena.
mn134:8-13.11: And how do you not falter amid presently arisen phenomena? …
mn134:8-13.12: That’s how you don’t falter amid presently arisen phenomena.
mn134:14.1: Don’t run back to the past,
mn134:14.6: you clearly discern in every case.
mn134:14.9: Today’s the day to keenly work—
mn134:14.10: who knows, tomorrow may bring death!
mn134:14.11: For there is no bargain to be struck
mn134:14.12: with Death and his mighty horde.
mn134:14.13: One who keenly meditates like this,
mn134:14.15: that’s who has one fine night—
mn134:14.19: Lomasakaṅgiya and One Fine Night is finished—the fourth.
